title: Finite stratified local cohomological bounds become global
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning a scheme with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $i_\alpha:S_\alpha\to X$ be a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] and choose a pro-étale covering $\{U_{\alpha j}\to S_\alpha\}_j$ on each stratum [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restrict coefficients by their actual exact inverse images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Suppose for each $\alpha,j$ there are integers $a_{\alpha j}\leq b_{\alpha j}$ such that $H^q(K|_{U_{\alpha j}})=0$ outside $[a_{\alpha j},b_{\alpha j}]$. Then one may select finitely many quasi-compact open subschemes of the covering members whose composites still cover each stratum, and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(K)=0$ for all $q\notin[a,b]$. One may take the minimum of the lower bounds and maximum of the upper bounds of their original covering members, with $[0,0]$ for an empty selected family. No flatness of $K$ and no dimension bound on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.3 and Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication; finite-cover boundedness argument. topology.tex Tag 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact); pro-étale covering definition and finite-stratum detection.

proof.text: Write the given finite affine covering as $X=\bigcup_{t=1}^N X_t$, with each coordinate ring Noetherian. Each $|X_t|$ is Noetherian by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], so every subset of it is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets]. An immersion identifies its source homeomorphically with its image, by the closed/open factorization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence $|S_\alpha|\cap |X_t|$ is quasi-compact. Restrict an arbitrary open cover of $S_\alpha$ to these finitely many intersections, choose a finite subcover on each, and take their union. This proves each $S_\alpha$ quasi-compact. The same argument with $S_\alpha$ replaced by $X$ proves $X$ quasi-compact in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. The given affine cover also makes $X$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]; thus $X$ satisfies the locally-Noetherian and quasi-compact hypotheses of the detection lemma used below.

source.place: Tag 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact), combined with properties.tex Tag 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology), and the given finite affine cover

proof.text: For each $\alpha$, take an affine open cover of the scheme $S_\alpha$ and choose a finite subcover $S_\alpha=\bigcup_{r=1}^{m_\alpha}V_{\alpha r}$ using step 1. Over each affine $V_{\alpha r}$ the covering condition of [sk-def-pe-site] supplies finitely many indices $j$ and affine opens $W_{\alpha rk}\subset U_{\alpha,j(\alpha,r,k)}\times_{S_\alpha}V_{\alpha r}$ mapping onto $V_{\alpha r}$; its affine-target refinement clause says this is a pro-etale covering of $V_{\alpha r}$. The displayed fibre product is the inverse-image open subscheme of the covering member, so each $W_{\alpha rk}$ is also an affine, hence quasi-compact, open subscheme of that original member. Zariski covers are pro-etale covers by [sk-def-pe-site]. Covering transitivity, axiom (ii) of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], therefore makes all $W_{\alpha rk}\to S_\alpha$ a covering. There are finitely many selected opens on each of finitely many strata. Empty strata require no selected opens.

source.place: Tag 0989 (definition-fpqc-covering), finite affine refinement; ordinary Zariski covers and the site covering-transitivity axiom

proof.text: Every restriction here uses the actual inverse-image ring, with no extension to a different ring. The inverse-image functors of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] are inverse images of the associated geometric morphisms. By [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact] they are exact also on modules over the inverse-image ring. Applied termwise to a representative of $K$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies their cohomology with inverse image of $H^q(K)$. This calculation is valid for an unbounded complex because kernels and images in a fixed degree use only its three adjacent terms. Iterated inverse image agrees with inverse image along the composite, by the composition clause (4) of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: the direct images are successive precompositions by base change, and their left adjoints are uniquely isomorphic. Thus restriction of $K|_{U_{\alpha j}}$ to a selected $W_{\alpha rk}\subset U_{\alpha j}$ is $K|_{W_{\alpha rk}}$, and it has zero cohomology outside the same original interval $[a_{\alpha j},b_{\alpha j}]$. This is also the exact termwise restriction convention of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction].

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), transported inverse-image coefficients; homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor) and derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)

proof.text: Let $T$ be the finite set of selected triples $(\alpha,r,k)$, retaining the label $j(\alpha,r,k)$ of the original covering member. If $T\ne\varnothing$, put $a=\min_{T}a_{\alpha,j(\alpha,r,k)}$ and $b=\max_{T}b_{\alpha,j(\alpha,r,k)}$. Since every selected lower bound is at most its upper bound, $a\le b$. If $q<a$, then $q<a_{\alpha,j(\alpha,r,k)}$ for every selected triple; if $q>b$, then $q>b_{\alpha,j(\alpha,r,k)}$ for every triple. Step 3 therefore gives $H^q(K|_{W_{\alpha rk}})=0$ whenever $q\notin[a,b]$. If $T=\varnothing$, put $a=b=0$; the same vanishing assertions on selected opens hold vacuously.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse-implication finite-stratification locality argument; elementary finite minimum/maximum bookkeeping made explicit

proof.text: Fix $q\notin[a,b]$ and let $F$ be the underlying abelian sheaf of $H^q(K)$. Step 3 identifies its inverse image to every selected $W_{\alpha rk}$ with the underlying sheaf of $H^q(K|_{W_{\alpha rk}})$, which is zero by step 4. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection] to the original finite stratification and to the coverings of its strata constructed in step 2. Its Noetherian hypothesis is verified in step 1, and it imposes no constancy condition on the ring sheaf. It gives $F=0$, hence $H^q(K)=0$: a module sheaf whose underlying abelian sheaf is zero has only the zero module structure. This also treats the empty selected family: the lemma applies to the empty coverings of the necessarily empty strata, so it gives vanishing in every degree. Thus the stated interval works globally, and no flatness, completeness, constructibility or dimension bound was used.

Step 3: exactness of inverse image on modules with transported scalars, and an exact functor commutes with cohomology; restricting to W keeps the member's interval. Step 4: elementary min/max. Step 5: the detection lemma is applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of H^q(K), with its hypotheses verified.
